prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core stance
- Make Scotland “stronger at Westminster” with a louder, progressive voice.
- Oppose austerity; never support putting the Conservatives in power; work with others to lock Tories out if there’s an anti‑Tory majority.
- Independence not on the ballot; focus on better UK governance and more powers for Scotland.

Economy and public finances
- Replace deep cuts with modest, responsible spending increases, prioritising investment in jobs, productivity and infrastructure; deficit and debt fall as a share of income.
- Fairer taxation: restore 50p top rate; bank levy/bonus tax; mansion tax; end non‑dom status; crack down on avoidance; review pension tax relief for the wealthiest.
- Create a sovereign wealth/energy fund when conditions allow.

Jobs, pay and business
- Raise UK minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the living wage; curb exploitative zero‑hour contracts.
- Capitalise a Scottish Business Development Bank; expand export finance; legal protections for prompt payment to small firms.
- Devolve and cut Air Passenger Duty by 50% (long‑term abolition); consider VAT cut for hospitality.
- Increase Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019–20; maintain strong investment allowances.

Public services, welfare and households
- NHS: increase UK health spending; £2bn extra for Scotland by 2020–21; protect from privatisation.
- Childcare: expand free nursery education to 30 hours a week for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds.
- Education: free university tuition; 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships; expand Educational Maintenance Allowance.
- Welfare: scrap Bedroom Tax; halt Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA→PIP; raise work allowance by 20%; overhaul sanctions and Work Capability Assessments; raise Carer’s Allowance to JSA level.
- Pensions: protect triple lock; single‑tier at £160/week; review rise beyond age 66; retain winter fuel allowance.
- Cut energy bills by funding ECO from general taxation and forcing pass‑through of wholesale price falls.

Housing and infrastructure
- Back a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes annually; invest in transport (including HS2 to and from Scotland), superfast broadband/4G and a broadband Universal Service Obligation.

Energy, climate and environment
- Oppose Trident renewal and new nuclear weapons; support a fracking moratorium.
- Boost renewables (offshore wind, hydro, CCS), Green Investment Bank, islands interconnector; reform transmission charging; expand community energy/heat; match Scotland’s carbon targets and create a Climate Justice Fund.
- Support species protection and action against the illegal ivory trade.

Rural, cities and sectors
- Fair share of CAP convergence uplift; simplify CAP; workable discard ban; devolve food levies.
- City Deals for all Scottish cities; £300m Scottish Cities Fund.
- Creative industries: fairer BBC Scotland funding (+£100m), Creative Content Fund, retain games tax relief.

Democracy, rights and policing
- Implement Smith Commission fully, then pursue Home Rule/full fiscal responsibility; devolve employment, welfare, business taxes, National Insurance and equality policy.
- Abolish House of Lords; adopt STV for elections; votes at 16–17; stronger MP recall.
- Protect Human Rights Act and ECHR; oppose “snoopers’ charter”; stronger rules on payday lending; devolve powers over fixed‑odds betting terminals.
- Equality: 50% women on public boards; mandatory equal pay reporting; tackle maternity discrimination; establish a Race Committee.

International, EU and defence
- Keep the UK in the EU; require a “double majority” for any exit; exempt NHS/Scottish Water from TTIP; restore post‑study work visas.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; improve aid quality; audit developing‑country debt; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy; recognise Palestine; require UN‑Charter‑based, Parliament‑approved military action.
- Defence: focus on High North/Arctic and cyber; more conventional capability in Scotland (MPA, patrol vessels); build Type 26 in Scotland; transparency on spend; stronger support for veterans.

Community safety and resilience
- Retain 1,000 extra police; seek VAT exemption for Police Scotland and Fire and Rescue; keep court fines revenue in Scotland; reinstate west‑coast emergency towing; return ARCC to Kinloss.
